breakdown.description: The prompt uses the polar moment J in the Euler buckling check, even though Euler buckling is governed by the flexural second moment I, not torsional rigidity.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification correctly uses I = π d⁴ / 64 (the second moment of area / flexural moment of inertia) for the Euler buckling calculation, not the polar moment J = π d⁴ / 32. There is no mention of J in the buckling check, matching the ground truth.

breakdown.description: The prompt treats a satisfactory average-stress yield check as if it ruled out buckling, even though a column may buckle before reaching the material yield stress.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification treats the yield check and the buckling check as two independent checks, and correctly concludes that even though the yield check passes (σ_avg < Sy), the column still fails by Euler buckling (P_cr < P). It does not treat a passing yield check as sufficient to rule out buckling, which aligns with the ground truth.
